headline: PM Tarique Rahman to visit Feni tomorrow for first time since taking office
summary: The Prime Minister will inaugurate a 1,542 crore BDT project for flood control and irrigation, and launch a rooftop solar power system for government buildings.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman will visit Feni tomorrow, Thursday, marking his first visit to the district since becoming Prime Minister. He will participate in several programs in the Parshuram and Fulgazi upazilas.

The Prime Minister is scheduled to arrive in Parshuram at 12:30 PM and inaugurate the 'Muhuri-Kahuya Flood Control, Drainage and Irrigation Project Rehabilitation (Phase 1)'. This project, approved by ECNA on June 16 this year, has a budget of 1,542.16 crore BDT.

The flood control project involves the rehabilitation of 67.92 km of embankments, 11.73 km of riverbank protection, re-excavation of 83.50 km of rivers and reservoirs, and the construction of 77 inlets. The work is expected to be completed by 2030.

In Fulgazi, the PM will visit Begum Khaleda Zia Women's College for a tree planting program at 1:30 PM. He will then proceed to the Fulgazi District Council Dak Bungalow to launch a 'rooftop solar' power supply system to the national grid.

The rooftop solar system has been installed on government buildings in Fulgazi, Parshuram, and Chhagalnaiya upazilas. This system, funded by the Feni Rural Electricity Society, provides approximately 1 megawatt of power, with 415 kW in Chhagalnaiya, 298 kW in Parshuram, and 249 kW in thegzip

At 3:00 PM, the Prime Minister will attend an event at the Fulgazi Government Pilot High School field, where he will distribute family cards, farmer cards, and honorariums to imams, muezzins, and khadems of religious places of worship.

Preparations for the visit are in the final stages, with a temporary helipad and public gathering space created in Parshuram. Security has been divided into red, yellow, and white zones to ensure safety and order.

headline: US Dollar poised for largest monthly rise against Euro in 14 months
summary: Strong US economic growth and rising interest rates drive the greenback higher, while Europe faces energy and debt concerns.
details: The US dollar is set to record its largest monthly increase against the euro in 14 months, rising nearly 2.5 percent in September. The surge is powered by robust US economic growth and expectations of rising interest rates.

In contrast, the euro has dipped to its lowest levels since May 2025, hitting $1.1312 on Tuesday. This decline is attributed to energy supply worries and political gridlock in France, where debt concerns are mounting ahead of next year's presidential election.
The stronger dollar has also impacted other currencies. The Australian dollar fell below 70 cents for the first time since early August, while the Swiss franc hit a 16-1/2 month low on Tuesday.
Market analysts suggest that the US economy is 'running hot' while Europe is losing the global AI race. Additionally, benchmark European gas prices recently spiked to their highest since 2022.
Investors are now closely watching Friday's US jobs report. A strong report could reinforce expectations that US interest rates will continue to rise, further strengthening the dollar.
Meanwhile, the Japanese yen has seen some recovery, with the dollar dropping 2 percent against the yen in September following US-Japan yen buying interventions and Japanese rate hikes.

The US dollar is set to record its largest monthly increase against the euro in 14 months, rising nearly 2.5 percent in September. The surge is powered by robust US economic growth and expectations of rising interest rates.

In contrast, the euro has dipped to its lowest levels since May 2025, hitting $1.1312 on Tuesday. This decline is attributed to energy supply worries and political gridlock in France, where debt concerns are mounting ahead of next year's presidential election.

The stronger dollar has also impacted other currencies. The Australian dollar fell below 70 cents for the first time since early August, while the Swiss franc hit a 16-1/2 month low on Tuesday.

Market analysts suggest that the US economy is 'running hot' while Europe is losing the global AI race. Additionally, benchmark European gas prices recently spiked to their highest since 2022.

Investors are now closely watching Friday's US jobs report. A strong report could reinforce expectations that US interest rates will continue to rise, further strengthening the dollar.

Meanwhile, the Japanese yen has seen some recovery, with the dollar dropping 2 percent against the yen in September following US-Japan yen buying interventions and Japanese rate hikes.
